cover.title: An open standard for digital chess
cover.lead: A strategic blueprint for portable identity, comparable ratings and shared integrity — without imposing a new platform.
cover.imageAlt: Marble chessboard with classic chess pieces

summary.title: Not another platform. One shared foundation.
summary.lead: The digital chess world is growing, but identity, reputation and game data remain locked within separate systems.
items: Separate identities, ratings and integrity decisions limit trust and choice.
A neutral standard connects existing platforms without replacing their distinctive character.
Players retain control; market participants compete on quality over shared infrastructure.

context.title: The market is growing. Trust is not keeping pace.
context.intro: The chess economy is heading towards doubling in size, while player profiles, ratings and reputation remain scattered across closed ecosystems. Growth without interoperability strengthens existing gatekeepers.
problems: Lichess, ChessBase and FIDE maintain separate identities, ratings and infrastructure.
Game history, connections and reputation do not currently move seamlessly with the player.
Network effects limit choice, innovation and a healthy digital chess culture.
context.conclusion: OCA will not become a fourth platform. It will be the neutral layer connecting existing strengths.

standard.title: From separate ecosystems to a single federated protocol
standard.intro: OCA does not take over functions. It defines the rules that enable existing participants to exchange identity, results and integrity information reliably.
standard.rolesTitle: Each participant brings a distinct strength.
roles: Maintains the standard, assesses compliance and safeguards the common interest.
Contributes open-source infrastructure and experience with public APIs.
Connects professional users, game archives and commercial applications.
Connects the standard with organised sport and official recognition.
standard.identityTitle: The player remains the source of trust.
standard.identityText: A Global_ID connects the trusted account to participating services. Personal data vaults keep history and consent under the player's control.
standard.quoteNote: That is why it belongs to the player.
standard.ratingTextA: Existing scores are not merely repackaged. The standard calculates a comparable rating from verified results within the federated network.
standard.ratingTextB: Independent modules share signals. A network-wide measure is taken only when two or more signals concur, with a transparent appeal process before an independent Fair Play Commission.

application.title: A digital protocol becomes a public resource only when people can use it.
application.intro: The standard becomes meaningful in settings where access, health and public digital infrastructure converge.
items: Chess Club in a Box brings together online play and local interaction.
Accessible chess programmes support social connection and mental activity.
Open standards align with public R&D, interoperability and the objectives of the Digital Markets Act.

execution.title: From establishment to a global standard
execution.intro: Four successive phases build legal legitimacy, technical functionality and public application in a controlled manner.
phases: Register a Belgian non-profit association (VZW) and sign the Founding Charter with core partners.
Define API standards and the open reference implementation.
Launch pilots in libraries and residential care homes in Flanders and the Netherlands.
Launch the OCA Rating worldwide and invite market participants to adopt the standard.
